c12_acc_cbse_02_003: Before averaging profits for goodwill, strip out one-off items, partner remuneration and abnormal income — you're estimating maintainable earnings, not just averaging raw numbers.
c11_acc_cbse_02_003: Purchased goodwill gets recorded because there's a real transaction proving its value; internal brand value has none. Ask: is there verifiable money evidence?
c12_acc_cbse_02_004: Capital employed isn't just total assets − current liabilities — exclude investments and fictitious assets, and adjust profits first. Check what's really business capital.
c11_acc_cbse_02_004: Going concern doesn't mean forever — just the foreseeable future. A loss-making firm can still be one if it has funding; check management's intent, not age or profit.
c12_acc_cbse_02_005: Revaluation method raises goodwill then writes it off; adjustment method never touches Goodwill Account — it settles through capitals. Check which the question asks for.
c11_acc_cbse_02_005: The period concept doesn't cause accrual — it creates the need to allocate, and accrual is the method that fulfils it. Trace the chain: going concern → periods → accrual.
c12_acc_cbse_02_006: An unrecorded asset is a gain: debit the asset, credit Revaluation. An unrecorded liability is a loss: debit Revaluation, credit the liability. Apply normal asset/liability logic.
c11_acc_cbse_02_006: Cost concept fixes the initial value, but depreciation can still adjust it later; dual aspect means at least two accounts — one transaction can touch three or more.
c12_acc_cbse_02_007: Accumulated reserves belong to the old partners — share them in the old ratio, not the new or sacrificing ratio. Ask: whose past effort built this up?
c11_acc_cbse_02_007: Matching isn't rupee-for-rupee — period costs like rent and depreciation match to the period that used them. And accrual tracks earning/incurring, not cash movement.
c12_acc_cbse_02_008: Capital adjustment isn't only the new partner's capital — all partners' capitals must align to the new ratio. Check which scenario the question describes before computing.
c11_acc_cbse_02_009: Consistency doesn't forbid change — you can switch methods if you disclose it. And full disclosure lives in the notes; contingent liabilities aren't balance-sheet items.
c12_acc_cbse_02_010: Match each item to its era: past items (revaluation, reserves) → old ratio; goodwill premium → sacrificing ratio; future capital alignment → new ratio.
c11_acc_cbse_02_010: Accrual follows the economic event, not the invoice — revenue counts when goods are delivered or service done, even if the bill comes next month.
c12_acc_cbse_02_011: When computing hidden goodwill, include the new partner's capital in the firm's total — their money becomes part of net assets on admission.
c11_acc_cbse_02_011: Accounting Standards aren't optional for companies — Sections 129/133 make them mandatory. Many still allow alternative treatments, which is why disclosure matters.
c12_acc_cbse_03_001: New ratio and gaining ratio aren't the same — gaining ratio is new minus old share. Compute each partner's gain separately before adjusting goodwill.
c11_acc_cbse_03_001: A business transaction must involve the firm exchanging value with an outside party — the proprietor's family dinner from a personal wallet doesn't count.
c12_acc_cbse_03_002: On retirement, goodwill adjusts in the gaining ratio — not the new ratio. The partner who gains more bears more; compute gain as new share minus old.
c11_acc_cbse_03_002: The supplier's invoice is the source document; the voucher is your firm's internal authorisation to record. One is external evidence, the other internal.
c12_acc_cbse_03_003: Revaluation (firm continues, old ratio) adjusts book values; Realisation (dissolution) records actual sales and payments. Check: is the firm closing or continuing?
c11_acc_cbse_03_003: Rent paid isn't paying off a liability — it reduces capital via expense. Only outstanding rent is a liability. Check: was the expense owed or just paid?
c12_acc_cbse_03_004: On retirement, reserves still go to all partners in the old ratio — the retiring partner earned their share of past accumulations. Don't use the new ratio here.
c11_acc_cbse_03_004: Debit and credit aren't just 'increase' and 'decrease' — a decrease in a liability is a debit. Always ask which account class is changing and on which side it lives.
c12_acc_cbse_03_005: The retiring partner's due isn't just the old capital balance — add goodwill, revaluation and reserves first, and treat the unpaid balance as a loan earning interest.
